# SB-1028 Safety bulletin: quench oil fire risk

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P3, line P3-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L4-RR01

## Hazard description

A potential ignition event has been identified associated with the quench oil lubrication system on the heat treat radial ring rolling mill EQ-P3-L4-RR01. The hazard arises when quench oil is introduced to heated surfaces or to an active hot work area without adequate containment and temperature management, creating an elevated flammability risk and the potential for a localized oil fire. Contributing factors observed during recent maintenance reviews and incident trend reviews include oil pooling at low points in the containment chassis, oil carried on external rotating surfaces, and transfer of oil to hot contact points during process disturbances. Any ignition on this equipment may rapidly involve machine structure, adjacent conveyor or material handling components, and stored combustible residues, leading to personnel injury and production loss.

Background: The radial ring rolling mill uses a lubricated quench oil delivery and return system that contacts components involved in rapid thermal exchange during normal operation. The lubricant part number for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) is CFW-LUB-315. The system includes reservoirs, supply lines, return lines, filters, and splash guards; failures or improper servicing of any of these elements can create flow deviations or unexpected oil exposure. Historical maintenance records and the maintenance manual indicate that oil system breaches and improper routing have been root causes in prior small-scale oil ignition events elsewhere in the facility. Refer to MM-P3-L4-RR01 for maintenance history and component diagrams; refer to SOP-P3-L4-01 and SOP-P3-L4-04 for established servicing and hot work procedures.

Rationale: This bulletin is issued to reduce the likelihood of oil contact with hot surfaces and to ensure controls are uniformly applied during operation, servicing, and hot work near the machine.

## Affected equipment

Primary: EQ-P3-L4-RR01 located on line P3-L4 at Plant P3.  
Secondary: Adjacent conveyors and material handling equipment within the same process cell where oil drainage or aerosolized oil could reach hot surfaces.  
Personnel: Operators, maintenance technicians, contractors performing any servicing, and any personnel performing hot work in the immediate area.

Scope: Controls and procedural changes described below apply to all activities that may expose hot surfaces to quench oil, including but not limited to routine servicing of the lubrication system, filter changes, reservoir top-offs, leak response, and any activities classified as hot work under site procedures.

## Required controls

Engineering controls
- Inspect and repair containment pans, splash guards, and return lines on EQ-P3-L4-RR01 to eliminate pooling and seepage paths. All repairs must restore watertight containment between oil-carrying components and machine hot surfaces.
- Re-route external oil lines to minimize proximity to heated housings and potential pinch points. Secure all external hoses and fittings to fixed structure; eliminate free-hanging sections that could contact rotating or heated parts.
- Install visible secondary containment beneath minimum leak points identified in MM-P3-L4-RR01. Secondary containment must be sized and positioned to intercept oil before it reaches the floor or adjacent hot zones.

Administrative controls
- Use only the specified lubricant: CFW-LUB-315 for EQ-P3-L4-RR01. Do not use substitute lubricants without documented approval from maintenance engineering and the process owner.
- Prior to any servicing activity that exposes oil-bearing components, confirm that the machine has been de-energized and cooled in accordance with SOP-P3-L4-01 and SOP-P3-L4-04. Servicing that requires heating of components or proximity to hot surfaces is prohibited unless the work is executed under a formal hot work permit and with full isolation of oil systems.
- Update the work permit and lockout-tagout procedures to include an explicit oil isolation checklist for EQ-P3-L4-RR01, referencing required containment verification steps.
- Prohibit open-flame or spark-producing activities inside the process cell unless the area has been inspected and cleared of oil contamination per hot work procedures in SOP-P3-L4-04.

Operational controls
- Operators must perform a pre-start oil system inspection on EQ-P3-L4-RR01 at the start of their shift to verify no visible leaks or oil pooling are present. Any abnormal condition requires immediate reporting to maintenance and removal of the machine from service until remediation.
- Implement increased frequency of visual checks after any maintenance that involves the lubrication system. Document findings in the equipment log described below.
- When responding to oil leaks, use absorbent materials rated for combustible liquids and collect used absorbents in sealed containers for proper disposal; do not leave saturated absorbents in process areas.

Training and PPE
- Provide targeted training to operators and maintenance personnel on the specific quench oil hazards associated with EQ-P3-L4-RR01 and on the use and limitations of personal protective equipment when responding to oil leaks or fires.
- Ensure that firefighting equipment appropriate for class B fires is present and accessible in the process cell, and that personnel assigned to respond have received training in its use.

Examples of failure modes and corrective action
- Example A: Oil accumulation in return pan leading to drip onto heated roll hub. Corrective action: Replace degraded pan, verify slope to drain, and add secondary containment as specified in MM-P3-L4-RR01.
- Example B: Hose chafing causing spray onto bearing housing near heated surface. Corrective action: Re-route hose, install abrasion sleeve, and secure with approved clamps; document in maintenance record.

## Records to keep

- Maintain a dedicated equipment log for EQ-P3-L4-RR01 that records pre-start inspections, leak reports, containment repairs, and any substitution requests for lubricant CFW-LUB-315. Include cross-reference to maintenance actions recorded under MM-P3-L4-RR01.
- Retain any hot work permits and clearance certificates issued in accordance with SOP-P3-L4-04 when work was performed near the oil system.
- Keep training completion records for personnel who receive the targeted quench oil hazard training. Include evidence of hands-on familiarization with containment and isolation checklists.
- Store photographic evidence of containment repairs and post-repair inspections in the equipment record for auditing purposes.

## Effective date

This bulletin is effective upon issue and applies to all activities on EQ-P3-L4-RR01 immediately. Compliance verification and initial auditing activities will be coordinated with maintenance and operations leadership and must reference MM-P3-L4-RR01, SOP-P3-L4-01, and SOP-P3-L4-04.

For questions or clarifications, contact the plant reliability engineer or the safety contact assigned to line P3-L4.
